scenes.headline: How Nanbeige4.2-3B loops its layers for depth
scenes.sub: A two-pass looped transformer, trained from scratch, then taught to act.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Pesto! Nanbeige four point two is a compact agent model, three billion parameters before embeddings, that runs its own layers twice. Here's how.

scenes.label: The idea
scenes.text: A looped transformer runs the same layers twice: compute depth grows, the parameter count doesn't. You pay for depth in FLOPs, not weights.
scenes.say: The idea: run the same layers twice. Compute depth grows, the parameter count doesn't. You pay for depth in compute, not in weights.

steps.say: A token climbs the transformer layers, then goes back through the very same layers a second time before the output head.

steps.note: about 75% of a standard model's token efficiency
steps.say: The report tested loop counts and landed on two, keeping roughly seventy-five percent of a standard transformer's token efficiency. More passes bought almost nothing.

steps.note: full KV cache on both passes
steps.say: Sharing the KV cache across passes would halve attention compute, but it consistently underperformed. So each pass keeps its full cache.

scenes.title: Why the loop is trained in

left.title: Upcycling
items: Convert it to a loop afterward
left.say: You could pretrain a normal model, then convert it into a looped one.

right.title: Looped from scratch
items: The loop is there for all 28T tokens
right.say: Nanbeige found training the loop from scratch, over twenty-eight trillion tokens, significantly better. The model adapts to reusing its layers.

scenes.title: Then post-training teaches it to act

items.say: Fine-tuning stretches the context window and slides the mix from reasoning toward acting.
A reward model removes repetitive, looping answers, which lifted agent scores too.
A penalty trims long reasoning on problems it already solves.
Then per-turn rubrics score every tool call, for denser credit over long tasks.

scenes.label: on SWE-Bench Verified, against 53.1 for Qwen3.5-9B
scenes.note: self-reported; public code benchmarks are the strongest signal
scenes.say: The public code benchmarks are the strongest signal: sixty-three point six on SWE-Bench Verified, self-reported, against fifty-three point one for a nine-billion Qwen.

scenes.text: Depth doesn't have to cost weights: trained in from scratch, a two-pass loop lets a small model reason deeper.
scenes.mark: Depth doesn't have to cost weights
scenes.say: Depth doesn't have to cost weights. Trained in from scratch, a two-pass loop lets a small model reason deeper.

recap: The same layers run twice, trained from scratch
Full KV cache kept on both passes
A four-stage post-training pipeline teaches it to act
scenes.say: To recap: one set of layers run twice, trained in from scratch, then taught to act.
